column1: # Game profile of Mega Man Legacy Collection (Switch, update 1.0.3 = v196608). Plays on the Mac: the collection's menus and Mega Man 1, with its display filters, at 60 fps
# Digital Eclipse's collection of the six NES Mega Man games (its NES emulation in main), SDK 3.7.0. It renders with NVIDIA's desktop OpenGL through EGL (subsdk0, not loaded): the host's GL
# layer implements it on Metal (dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m). Its shaders are GLSL ES files in the RomFS (shaders/nx/*.glsl: the sprite, CRT and composite filters) and two strings in main, which
# dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py translates offline; the host finds each by the hash of its text

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk. subsdk0 is NVIDIA's OpenGL driver, which programs the GPU through NvRm: never loaded, the GL layer answers main's EGL and GL calls
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory; main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB, a 3328 MB heap region. The Mac footprint in a stage
# no NVN shaders: the NVN tables stay empty (gl_shaders.py writes the GL library and its table, not the profile)

column2: Mega Man Legacy Collection has no NVN shaders (its GLSL shaders go through the GL layer)
